title: Make Them an Offer They Can’t Refuse

 Before you drop a number on a business, learn to think like the original deal pros.

 Make Them an Offer They Can’t Refuse
Hi Sara,
When it comes to making offers on a business, you don’t want to come off like a clueless rookie. You want to come in cool, calculated, and compelling.
So I created a framework to help you do exactly that. And yes, it’s called M.A.F.I.A.—because who understands business negotiation better than the original entrepreneurs in pinstripes?
Here’s how to make your offer bulletproof (and maybe a little intimidating—in a good way):
M – Market Demand:
Is it a buyer’s market or a seller’s market? That shiny accounting firm might look unreasonably expensive in May but be 80% of the cost by December. Timing is everything.
A – Adjusted EBITDA:
This isn’t just about the profit number in the listing. You need to adjust for reality—like whether you’ll be replacing an owner-operator. Because spoiler: hiring someone who knows what they’re doing is not simple and if you do pull it off, it costs money, and that affects your real returns.
F – Financing Realities:
Please, I beg you—don’t offer a price you can’t actually fund. You need to know if you’re using SBA, cash, seller finance (rare), or investor capital. Pitching a fantasy offer just wastes everyone’s time. Bonus points if you don’t offer terms the bank won’t allow.
I – Industry Multiples:
If this is the first time you’re hearing “industry multiple,” stop reading and go Google it. Every industry has them. Don’t offer based on gross revenue unless you want zero leverage when the actual profit numbers look different in diligence. Tie your offer to EBITDA or SDE and show your work.
A – Asking Price:
Buyers often obsess over financials but forget the most important number in the deal: the seller’s real asking price—which has just as much to do with emotions and legacy as dollars. If your offer doesn’t reflect what the seller actually cares about, don’t be surprised when you lose the deal to someone who simply paid more attention.
Follow these steps, and you’ll go from looking like a hopeful buyer to a serious contender.

To offers that don’t get laughed off the table,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder, Deal Academy
